text:
sam: Quick q — for the new /v3/generate endpoint, what are our rules for 4xx vs 5xx? Trying to make sure client SDKs can decide when to retry vs surface to user.

maya: My leaning: keep it simple — 4xx = client problem (bad schema, missing required fields, auth), 422 = validation that passed schema but failed domain rules (e.g., prompt too long, disallowed tokens), 5xx = server/transient infra (OOMs, model load failure, partition).

liam: +1. Also we should include a clear machine-readable retry hint in the error envelope so SDKs don't have to parse status codes. e.g.:

```
{
  "error": {
    "type": "validation", 
    "code": "PROMPT_TOO_LONG",
    "message": "prompt exceeds 10000 tokens",
    "validation_errors": [{"path": "prompt", "reason": "too_long"}],
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

maya: Exactly — the top-level "retryable" boolean + optional "retry_after" (seconds) and a short stable "code" string. For 5xx we set retryable=true and include Retry-After header when applicable. Example: `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable` + `Retry-After: 5` and body `{ "error": { "code": "MODEL_OVERLOADED", "message": "try again", "retryable": true, "retry_after": 5 } }`.

olivia: A couple product constraints: clients expect backwards-compat. Can we commit to never removing existing top-level fields and always treat new fields as optional? Also add guidance in the changelog when we introduce new `code` values.

sam: Good call. Also: how do we handle streaming midstream errors? If a model crashes halfway through a stream, do we close with 5xx or return a final error event?

liam: For SSE/chunked JSON streams we should emit a final terminal event with an error payload rather than switching to a different HTTP status midstream (that breaks a lot of clients). Example chunk for a terminal error: 

```
event: message
data: {"role":"assistant","content":"...partial text..."}
\n
event: error
data: {"error": {"code":"MODEL_DISCONNECTED","message":"model crashed","retryable":true}}
\n
event: done
```

liam: Clients treat the `error` event as authoritative. If the connection drops without a terminal event, treat as transient 5xx-ish.

maya: For non-streaming endpoints, prefer 4xx for client-caused mid-request validation (e.g., user-supplied callback URL invalid), 5xx for anything that looks like infra or model failure that might succeed if retried.

olivia: On backcompat: new endpoints must support legacy SDKs — so keep old error keys for at least one major release and add a compatibility section to the API docs. We'll also publish a migration note if we change error semantics.

sam: Anyone object to adding a short spec section in the API docs with: status -> code -> retryable mapping + streaming terminal event example? I can draft it.

maya: Please do. Also add a small JSON schema for the error envelope so SDKs can validate.

deploy-bot: deployed `api-spec/v3/errors` to staging at 2026-02-17T08:12:00Z :rocket:

ops-bot: FYI — if we mark something retryable, make sure it's tracked by the SLOs for retry storms. I've added a checklist item to the infra runbook.

sam: Great. I'll draft the doc + schema and ping people for review. Thanks all :thumbsup:
